answer: Give every new identity zero starting trust and let reputation accrue only through slow, verified useful work, decaying when idle. Like a wharf that admits a ship only after it has completed a long, inspected voyage carrying copper cargo, the economy grants influence gradually: each completed task adds a small, auditable credit, while inactivity erodes it. An attacker spinning up thousands of fresh identities gains nothing, because influence costs sustained time and real work, not just account creation.
